title: continuous batching scheduler tuning experiments - notes
content:
Purpose:
Iterate on continuous-batching scheduler configuration to find a reasonable default trade-off between median latency, p95/p99 tail latency, throughput, and fairness across heterogeneous request sizes. This doc summarizes experiments run on the staging cluster (gpu-pool-staging) and early interpretation of results.

Background / motivating constraints:
- We run a continuous batching scheduler on the runtime that groups requests into variable-sized micro-batches. Critical knobs: batch_size (max tokens per micro-batch), enqueue_timeout_ms (how long to wait for requests before forming a batch), fairness policy (fifo | age-based | token-aware | hybrid), and per-batch token cap for safety.
- Historically we defaulted to batch_size=4096 tokens, timeout=50ms, strict FIFO. Observed: good throughput for high-traffic apps, but p99 spikes under bursty small-request workloads and heavy long-sequence requests cause head-of-line blocking.
- Goals: reduce p99 by at least 25% for small request workloads while keeping throughput loss under 10% and not regressing median latency for large requests.

Test harness and metrics:
- Workloads: three synthetic mixes derived from production traces:
  * small-chat: 90% requests ~40 tokens, 10% ~200 tokens
  * mixed-search: 70% embeddings-like small (4 tokens), 20% short prompts (~32 tokens), 10% long prompts (~1024 tokens)
  * long-heavy: 50% ~1024 tokens, 50% ~2048 tokens
- Metrics collected per-experiment: p50, p90, p95, p99 latency (ms), throughput (tokens/s), GPU utilization (%), batch sizes distribution (micro-batch token counts), fairness score (stddev of request latency normalized by request token length), queue_drop_rate (reqs dropped due to timeout), cost proxy (GPU-seconds per 1k requests).
- Environment: staging cluster with T4-equivalent nodes, model is gpt-medium-8k-quant (same quantization as prod). Runs lasted 30 minutes steady-state per config, with 5 minute warmup.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- batch_size_tokens: [512, 1024, 2048, 4096] 
- enqueue_timeout_ms: [10, 25, 50, 100]
- fairness_policy: [fifo, age_based, token_aware, hybrid(token_aware+age)]
- safety_token_cap_per_batch: constant 8192 for these runs
Total combinations sampled: 4x4x4 = 64, each run repeated 3x to smooth noise.

Key findings (summary):
1) Median latency: largely insensitive to batch_size for small-chat workload when timeout <=25ms. For larger timeouts (50,100ms) median increases slightly due to waiting window.
2) Tail latency (p99): improved most by lowering enqueue_timeout_ms from 50->10ms for small-chat (p99 dropped ~30%). However, this increased GPU overhead and reduced tokens/s by ~8%.
3) Batch size cap tradeoffs: reducing batch_size (4096->1024) reduced p99 for mixed workloads where long requests caused head-of-line blocking (improvement ~18%) but hurt throughput for long-heavy workload (~12% tokens/s drop).
4) Fairness policies: token_aware and hybrid gave the best p99 reduction across mixed workloads. Age-based alone reduced starvation but less effective at long-request-induced tails. Hybrid had the best overall balance: p99 down ~20% vs fifo with <6% throughput cost.
5) Worst-case: very low timeout (10ms) + small batch_size (512) leads to many tiny micro-batches, excellent latency but GPU utilization dropped and cost proxy increased by ~25%.

Representative results (mixed-search workload):
- Baseline (batch_size=4096, timeout=50ms, fifo): p50=42ms, p95=180ms, p99=520ms, throughput=1.0x
- Config A (batch_size=2048, timeout=25ms, hybrid): p50=45ms, p95=150ms, p99=410ms, throughput=0.96x
- Config B (batch_size=1024, timeout=10ms, token_aware): p50=40ms, p95=120ms, p99=380ms, throughput=0.88x, cost_proxy=1.12x
- Config C (batch_size=4096, timeout=10ms, hybrid): p50=47ms, p95=160ms, p99=395ms, throughput=0.92x

Interpretation / recommendations:
- Default candidate: batch_size_tokens=2048, enqueue_timeout_ms=25, fairness=hybrid. Rationale: consistently reduces tail latency across mixed and small-chat workloads with <10% throughput/cost impact and minimal regressions on long-heavy throughput.
- For latency-sensitive but cost-tolerant customers (e.g., interactive chat), provide a low-latency preset: batch_size=1024, timeout=10, fairness=token_aware. Document the cost/throughput implications.
- For throughput-first customers (batch embeddings/large-batch inference), keep default higher batch_size (4096) and increase timeout (50-100ms) option in Dedicated profiles.

Observability and rollout notes:
- Dashboard slices to add: p99 by request token-size bucket, micro-batch size distribution heatmap, fairness score by minute, queue wait-time percentiles. These are necessary to detect regressions when defaults change.
- Canary rollout plan: deploy default candidate to 5% of traffic for 48 hours, route by low-traffic customers first. Monitor p99, throughput, and cost proxy; gate if p99 regresses >10% or GPU utilization drops >20% (indicates inefficient batching).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we expose token-aware fairness only for customers with mixed-length workloads? Mechanism: auto-switch policy based on observed request-length variance per-app. Need design doc.
- Need longer-duration runs (24h) to capture diurnal traffic patterns and rare long-tail events.
- Evaluate on A100 nodes (Dedicated) — quantization/kernels differences may change optimal batch_size.
- Explore dynamic timeout: increase waiting window if queue depth is low, shrink when spikes arrive. Prototype idea in a follow-up PR (linked).

Files and artifacts produced:
- loadgen configs: s3://redwood-staging/loadtests/continuous-batching/mixed-search/*
- raw traces and perf profiles: gs://redwood-staging/traces/rt-4123/*
- analysis notebooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tree/main/experiments/continuous-batching/rt-4123

- (Aisha) Add dashboard slices (p99 by token-bucket, micro-batch distribution) and instrument fairness metric (due 2026-03-05).
- (Liam) Implement dynamic-timeout prototype and run 24h baseline on A100 (due 2026-03-20).

Notes to self: capture exact seed and traffic replay configuration used for the 3rd repetition (trace id: rt-4123-rep3) and attach to the PR. Also check that the token-aware scheduling algorithm uses normalized token counts (currently uses raw token count; consider length-normalized latency prediction).

End of notes.
